use: Roll the ballpoint down both name seams.
reading: It catches after the K on Kip’s cuff. On the spare it rolls straight across the K. One name was sewn into the cloth. The other was pressed into it.
speaker: optics-nim
offer: Give Nim the two different Ks.
reply: Nim puts her own cuff under the press. “You can carry the mark of someone who never wore you.” She leaves the pressed cuff on a dummy for the next audience.

use: Lay the lens ring over the two dates.
reading: The inner date is the day the pear buttons arrived. The later ink entered the price under Kip’s name. A week of wear sits nowhere on the slip.
speaker: scholar-sefa
offer: Ask Sefa about the unpriced week.
reply: “Seven suppers,” Sefa says. “He sat with me at two. The other five belong to somebody else’s memory.” She hums the tune she sang at the second one.

use: Slide the brass plate behind the coat rail.
reading: The square notch releases a door narrow enough for one shoulder. On the inside its latch is a soft loop. Whoever needs to leave in a hurry can pull without waking the hall.
speaker: warden-ise
offer: Bring Ise the measurement of the inside latch.
reply: “I asked for a latch low enough to reach from a chair.” Ise takes off her badge and tries the loop sitting down. “Good. It still works.”

use: Set the moth lamp on the floor and wait.
reading: A glimmermoth goes under the hanging coat. Half a wing reappears through the wall. Behind the rail a door has been painted the colour of plaster.
speaker: optics-nim
offer: Give the understudy the moth’s entrance.
reply: Nim sends the moth through first. For once the audience watches the little light instead of her hands. She gets to choose the instant she steps out.

use: Turn the cut glass sideways through both pears.
reading: Light splits at a bubble in the pear on Kip’s cuff. The chipped green pear on the spare throws one narrow shadow. It has a flat back like a stamp.
speaker: smith-hesper
offer: Show Hesper the flat-backed pear.
reply: “Button mould. Somebody wore the stamp to save pocket space.” Hesper laughs. She turns her own apron out and three little washers fall on the floor.

use: Put the stone on the curling bottom corner.
reading: Under the curl are the words “deduct one ferry fare”. Kip had drawn a fine angry moustache on the printed pear. He still has to get home.
speaker: kip-arden
offer: Give Kip the loose fare line without smoothing away his drawing.
reply: “You left the moustache!” Kip copies the fare line onto his ticket and keeps the original pear for himself. “I’ll ask at the window. You can stand by. Just stand.”

use: Put the guild weight on the counter scale.
reading: The price tag stamped CLOTH swings up before the pan balances. It was printed for wool sold by weight. Somebody used it to charge a flat fare.
speaker: warden-ise
offer: Give Ise the weight behind the coat price.
reply: Ise takes the fare table down for the afternoon. A driver has to wait for change. Kip gets to point out the two unlike units himself.

use: Mesh Mara’s loose cog with the ticket stamper.
reading: At half a turn it stamps one pear. At a full turn the same piece of paper has two. Mara counts the wet prints, then takes one finger off the counter lever.
speaker: kip-arden
offer: Let Kip turn the double-stamp himself.
reply: Kip gets two pears on one receipt and four on another. “How many coats am I wearing now?” He copies the first pair. That joke will fit on one ticket.

use: Hold the market notice against the price tag.
reading: Both have the same stop after “keeper”. The little line after it belongs to the keeper who takes in a bundle. Reading straight across would charge the next wearer.
speaker: warden-ise
offer: Ask Ise where the keeper’s sentence ends.
reply: Ise reads both ways. At the second reading she stops rubbing her thumb over her own name. “I can initial that change. It was my line.”

use: Fit the splinter under the gilt tag.
reading: The lift exposes a paler pear. The price was pinned over an older offer to mend cuffs. The older sign gives a different reason for leaving a coat here.
speaker: optics-nim
offer: Send Nim the offer that sat under the price.
reply: Nim puts the old offer over the costume peg. A driver leaves a sleeve for repair on his way home. He has never once been to a play.

use: Catch a drop from each cuff in the little pot.
reading: Before rain touches the roof, the spare lets go three drops. The third one lands when the hand over the speaking pipe taps twice. The pot keeps the sound distinct.
speaker: optics-nim
offer: Give Nim a three-drop cue she can hear with her back turned.
reply: “Again. I can do that one with my eyes on the child.” Nim catches the third drop in her palm and opens the curtain with her other hand.

use: Walk Kip’s warm-step route under the hem of the awning.
reading: The official ticket puts the cloakroom indoors. Kip’s route reaches the same hook from the street, even after the name desk shuts. A damp footprint stops there.
speaker: kip-arden
offer: Let the mapmaker lead the late way home.
reply: Kip gives you the slow tour. The third step makes the squeak of a very small duck. “There,” he says. “Now you could find it in the dark without me.”

use: Frame the wet sleeve and then the hand above it.
reading: In the narrow frame a dry actor cries rain. Widen it and a second hand squeezes a sponge. Nim holds both pictures still long enough for a child to see who did the work.
speaker: scholar-sefa
offer: Let Sefa put the unseen hand in the song.
reply: Sefa gives the sponge a whole verse. The child who worked it objects to “silver rain”. It was ordinary dishwater. They keep that rhyme.

use: Ring one note behind the drawn curtain.
reading: The bell carries through the speaking pipe to the hook. A listener can ask for a coat without facing the whole waiting room. Nim leaves her end unplugged.
speaker: warden-ise
offer: Offer Ise the far end of the bell.
reply: “I used to insist people came to the front.” Ise moves her stool to the pipe. A quiet sleeve comes through. She offers a dry one without looking up.

use: Run the red and gold threads to the two cuffs.
reading: The gold thread reaches the squeeze bulb. The red one stops at a hand-sewn repair. One explains the downpour in the show. The other belongs to a night somebody actually got wet.
speaker: scholar-sefa
offer: Send Sefa the two ends without tying them together.
reply: She ties one to the stage bill and the other to the repair book. “Two true ends,” she says. “A knot in the middle would tell a lie.”

use: Trace the ferryman’s chalk under the cast list.
reading: A ferry-cant mark asks someone to save a warm place until a late arrival. Its line runs past the name column. Nobody has to claim to be an actor to need it.
speaker: scholar-sefa
offer: Read the late-arrival mark aloud to Sefa.
reply: “My father would put a bowl there before you finished that word.” Sefa sets a bowl on the warm step. You hear her ask first whether anyone wants soup.

use: Pay the measuring knot out along the clothesline.
reading: From the wings the line stops short of the public peg. From the inside landing it reaches. Someone in the lining can pass a coat without stepping into the scene.
speaker: warden-ise
offer: Show Ise how far the inside hand can reach.
reply: She fits the hook where the knot landed. The next visitor can hand clothes through from a seat. Ise finds another place to hang her badge.

use: Leave the weather glass under the roof while the cuff drips.
reading: The glass holds steady. A warm hand at the top of the sleeve starts another little shower. It settles what can happen inside this theatre. Kip’s first three drops still need a witness.
speaker: kip-arden
offer: Tell Kip which rain you managed to repeat.
reply: “Good. I can stop saying I saw a storm.” He opens his pocket. “I still saw a drop land on this pear. You can keep the storm bit open.”

use: Turn the shard until both notices are legible.
reading: Two scraps say that Kip left a coat. Their crooked comma and missing T are identical. One notice was copied from the other before either witness arrived.
speaker: scholar-sefa
offer: Give Sefa the one source behind two voices.
reply: Sefa cuts the chorus down to one singer. It sounds lonelier. “Good,” she says. “One neighbour can still have something worth hearing.”

use: Set the worn reach of the rope beside the public hook.
reading: The hook height was copied from a standing keeper’s shoulder. Three turns lower it far enough for a seated hand. The hem still clears the puddle below.
speaker: kip-arden
offer: Give Kip a hook he can adjust from the floor.
reply: He lowers it for a stranger and puts the end back in her hand. “You can put it exactly where you like. Mine was too high.”

use: Fold the survey slip to match the signed return.
reading: The forms counted people who stopped at the desk. Somebody passing a coat through the lining had no box to mark. A full page of signatures could miss an entire night.
speaker: warden-ise
offer: Ask Ise to count the quiet night without naming sleepers.
reply: She sets one jar each side of the pipe for dry and wet buttons. “I can buy enough wool with that. A person’s name was never the price of a button.”

use: Set the wax copy beside the price stamp.
reading: The outer rings match. The coat receipt has no inner cut. The Guardian seal travelled as a copied picture. No wearer signed either circle.
speaker: optics-nim
offer: Let Nim show the audience what the seal can actually do.
reply: Nim stamps a paper pear and passes it along the whole back row. Everybody has an excellent pear. Nobody has acquired a coat.

use: Follow the citation thread back from the bill.
reading: The receipt points to Vesper’s wardrobe gift. The gift note calls the spare “for the person who brings the first one back”. It does not say who that person will be.
speaker: optics-nim
offer: Read Vesper’s last seven words with Nim.
reply: Nim turns the line into a part anybody can play. Tonight the person who brings the coat back is the woman who wrings out the sponge. She gets the last bow.

use: Dust the inside handle with a pinch of soot.
reading: A return spring pulls two narrow arcs through the dust. On the public side the handle hardly moves. The latch opens from inside even when the desk seems shut.
speaker: smith-hesper
offer: Give Hesper the sweep of the hidden spring.
reply: She bends a loop so the spring will answer a lighter pull. “Had my hands full once,” she says. She tries it with both fists full of cloth.
